body.p: At night, enemies came to Shiktovul and started shooting at people who were sleeping, people like that. Shiktovul was barefoot, he grabbed his shoes and jumped out of the tent. His skis were hanging outside. He took [the naked skis], went barefoot [on skis], he hardly got out [of their hands] at night. They shoot at him at night, in Shiktovul. He keeps getting away [from them], he keeps looping around. His younger brother is such a brave man, he is looking round for his younger brother. He didn't find him. He didn't find him. He didn't find his little brother's trace. He ran straight away. There he put on his shoes, put them on, and after staying [a little], he ran [on skis]. His brother hid. He hid, they [the tramps?] then realised. The tramps didn't look properly. He immediately left [from them]. He also put on skis - where, shoes, hiding, putting on. Then he immediately ran away. So, the people saw - he also left [from the tramps]. They called him Taktakan, Shiktowul's brother. He also came out from the other side. He was looking for the trace of his elder brother. He came a little before he got here. He said, "My brother was killed here by those you let in!" Taktakan managed to shoot them. He returned: he had come in vain. Then, returning, he did not manage to kill [them]. The people shot him. The children were not killed, all the boys were killed. As they killed, they asked each other: ''Is there no Shiktowul now?" "No!" "They didn't kill them and their father, did any of them escape?" They left, there were three of them. They found them - when there were few families left, they killed them. Three or four families. These they killed. If their milara (?) were far away, they came from far away. They went and started searching again. They found the brave Khochenko. One family was starving. Shiktovul says: â"What for!" Immediately the long Khochenko killed [the reindeer?]. He, Nyurgucho, is always hungry. Shiktowul says: "Well, let us eat, if you are hungry!" They killed a fat reindeer - they were hungry. Khochenko started looking for the reindeer. He found it. He saw it and turned back [i.e. ran away]. They saw their fire. He led (?) his family out. There the people were [lit. there they were the people?], there his family went, to the reindeer. He came, he crept up, he found out how to creep up, how to approach - they didn't see him coming. Khochenko began to say: "Nyurgucho, isn't that you? Dyuduwul, is that you?" "Shiktowul, is that you?" Shiktowul lies down. Shiktowul replies: "Eh, it's me, it's me!" He's covered in boils, they took their arrows from Dyuduwul. Shiktowul says: "Eh, don't do that! He wanted to talk to Shiktowul, to speak. I made my Khochenko act (?). They didn't eat, they started chasing; they took their bows, they started chasing. Dyuduwul stayed behind. He went home, caught up - only the tent [not put up, lit. what they make a tent with] - [no one] is there, his family ran away. Shiktowul ran away, he is looking, catching up. He ran past Khochenko, [he] is not in the house. He started to catch up - he can't catch up in a good way. He stayed, [no longer] does not do it [does not catch up]. He found families there, which he looked out for while chasing after Khochenko. The big Khochenko started bullying Shiktowul, they started shooting at each other. They shot at each other until they ran out of their arrows. Shiktowul ran out [of arrows]. Khochenko ran out [of arrows]. Khochenko ran. Shiktowul loaded [his quiver] with arrows, something to shoot with; [they] searched for a long time. They found Shiktowul in chase and asked: "Where has Khochenko gone [lit. where has he become]?." Shiktowul says: "Where should he be? He's gone!" They say to Shiktowul: "Friends, will you not do more? We will go to another." Shiktowul chased [after them], he ran and found him there, he went to his family. At first Shiktowul thought - now they [had] run out. But he still had some arrows. Again they got into a fight, again they started shooting at each other. Again they ran out of arrows at the same time. He, Khochenko, ran away again. When he ran out of arrows, Shiktowul reloaded [put in the quiver] what he was going to shoot with, reloaded the arrows. He went there in pursuit, chased, caught up there. Khochenko again [fought with him], he still had arrows. They opened fire again. This time they opened fire again, for the third time. Shiktowul thought: "Well, now [the arrows] have run out, I guess!" He loaded the arrows [in his quiver], and again set off in pursuit. He caught up with the people who [saw this], they shouted. He heard the people, they shouted: "Shiktowul, Shiktowul!" The people immediately understood. The people met [him] with arrows, heard by the stomping. Khochenko, they said; they understood at once. The people understood at once. Shiktowul ran away. Since then Shiktowul has not come to this people. Khochenko was tired. Shiktowul was tired - he left the people. Shiktowul left then. He went to meet his comrade, he met Dyuduwul. "Are you all going?" Dyuduwul began to say: "Where did he come from? Whence have you appeared, have you travelled much?" What are you doing now - you these ones were not here?" Well, he left [them] - a lot of people. That year they left like that. That year they left [them] like that. In winter they were left alone, they went to fight again. They found two families - they killed them. They left two girls [alive]. Only Shiktowul wanted to kill [them]. Nyurgucho said: "We won't, we won't [kill them?]!" "Well, we won't [kill] them!" Shiktowul thinks - that's right; the soul is good. He said to those girls: "You wish to do good to Shiktowul!" They stayed there for a while. They took off Shiktowul's shoes. Shiktowul says: "You, come back! I really want a woman - wait [lit. don't (leave)], let's sleep properly!" The women - that's how they were. She says [one of them]: "It is good for me!" The other also says: "It is good for me too!" Shitkowul said: "It will be good!" They left and went with the women. At night they stopped to spend the night. The woman hit [ Shiktowul] with a shoe, with an axe, she hit him. He shouted: "She wanted to kill me!" The woman who hit ran away; the other one jumped out. He took a knife, chased after her, pushed her, caught up with her. The one who pretended (?) to be asleep, he killed as if he were. "No [not killed yet]! I will kill her!" "Don't do that! You didn't do it much!" He brought her, this woman. "Where to? You gonna try to kill again?" "No!" He said: "Now we're going to kill you!" Another [time] he said: "Well, I'm not going to [kill]!" He didn't kill. After that he did not do it again. Then they said: "If you dare to kill Nyurgucho's women, we will kill you!" He was afraid. They didn't kill him - they became good. Shiktowul left again, he started to wander. He guarded them. They would go for something, go for something, look for something, go out to get something [to buy?]. Shiktowul would look and kill that person. They became afraid. The people then began to live together. Shiktowul waited [guarded]. He left again at some moment. He kills someone again. He killed this person alone. He did not appreciate everyone, he split off. He went back, found a comrade - he says: "Bring him to the middle of the path!" "It's far!" He doesn't want to lead him! He doesn't talk [to Shiktowul]. The night has come. Shiktowul said - thinking: âShall I now kill the one who has fallen asleep?" "Does he want to kill me?" Shiktowul has thought of a way to kill him. "There, where he will kill me?!" The [comrade] became angry He [ Shiktowul] began to guard. Before going to bed, he went out to urinate - Shiktowul was on guard. He went quietly to the matchmakers - Shiktowul is watching. He went, quickly, he went quickly, he ran. Shiktowul took his arrows and went in pursuit - he killed [ a comrade]. Shiktowul killed him, he thought he would kill him when they went to bed. Then he killed him. After that went back, was coming back. He thought, he thought: "Where is his family?" He didn't go to people, he didn't want to go to his own, he was afraid. He killed in vain, he was afraid. He was hungry. He found a man who was skinning a wild reindeer. He was hungry. He crept up to the skinned [reindeer]; he crept up and shot past him. Not good this time. The one now thinks - who? Isn't it Tokshiwul? Tokshiwul - his son. Shiktowul [ proviso: Tokshiwul?] asks the sneak: â"Shiktowul, is that you?" "Eh, it's me!" Tokshiwul looks closely: "Father! You're alive!" Tokshiwul stopped putting the meat in. "Alive!" He thought he was dead, but it turned out that his father was alive. He became a human being, he stopped suffering from hunger, he stopped. He quenched his hunger [lit. opened his mouth hungry]. [Tokshiwul] led his father home. His wife asked: "How [lit. where?] do you live?" Shiktowul said: "I live!" The wife began to ask: "Will you pay there?" "From where? I have not [paid off] for Tokshakan?! There are none who know me - there were shamans. There, far away, they were. The shamans, wanted to [kill me]. Being shamans, they stopped. They gave up and now the other two stones will not pay. I didn't pay for four people (?). Then how many there were [people?], then we all paid off." Shiktowul fell asleep - their fire was burning. Tokshiwul hung up his shoes to dry. People gathered [around] to kill [Shiktowul]. They began to ask, in order to kill [him]: "Shiktowul, is it you?" Shiktowul said: "Eh, its me!" "How old you have become!" "It's me - I've lived!" As he lay, so he lies. As soon as he lay down, they killed him. Tokshiwul took his shoes, took herbs for insoles and jumped out and took his knife. With his knife Thokshiwul scattered the people; the people who were standing in a crowd [lit. face to face?]. They wanted to shoot, but they didn't manage to do it. The people scattered. He jumped out, he ran away with a knife. When he got to the middle, they were chasing him - he hid in a hollow tree. This one is also like his father. They caught up with his father; they said they chased him for a long time, he fell behind. His legs ached. He climbed up. You couldn't see him - he put on his shoes. He put on his shoes. He became visible, but they were still chasing Tokshiwul. He escaped, he ran, he didn't have a single arrow, he had a single knife. He ran again. Then he had already put on his shoes. Then they stopped the chase. The behaviour, everything is just like his father. The behaviour, everything is just like his father. Shiktowul is from the Turumbi clan, Khochenko is from the Barkhakhan [the other side] clan.
